inspiration: Palette remap tables: one sprite set is recoloured for variants and for effects such as a dimmed pause screen by swapping colour indexes through a table, not by repainting. Ref: assets/plrgfx/warrior/whu/whulm.trn and assets/gendata/pause.trn (names only; not opened).
Indexed run-length sprites with one shared palette: sprites are stored as compact indexed frames, so transparent areas cost almost nothing. Ref: assets/gendata/cutl1dw.clx (not opened).

Animation as a data table: each creature row gives a sprite width, an image name and six animation slots, each with a frame count and a frame rate. Animation is tuned in a spreadsheet, not in code. Ref: assets/txtdata/monsters/monstdat.tsv (header line and row structure).

Loot by prefix and suffix: item names and stats are built from a prefix table and a suffix table, with unique items kept in a separate table. Lots of variety from little art. Ref: assets/txtdata/items/item_prefixes.tsv, item_suffixes.tsv and unique_itemdat.tsv.

One dungeon per floor as a tile-index file: each floor is a separate map file and the town is its own file, which keeps floors easy to swap. Ref: assets/levels/l1data/ and assets/levels/towndata/automap.dun.

Storyboard stills with portrait frames: a short run of wide stills and cropped portrait frames carries a cutscene with very little animation. Ref: assets/gendata/cutportrw.clx and cutstartw.clx (names only; not opened).

Hellfire as an add-on folder: the expansion lives in mods/hf with its own manifest and overrides for maps, art and text, so a mod can ship new content without changing the base game. Ref: mods/hf/manifest.ini.

briefs.label: Armour-tint hero set
briefs.why: One body animation with several colour tables gives many armour looks for the cost of one set of frames.
briefs.keep: Shared frames; one colour-remap table per armour variant; a clear base body.
briefs.change: Our own silhouette and shoulder ornament; our own tints (no metal names); a different head and crest design.
briefs.ref: assets/plrgfx/warrior/whu/whulm.trn and whufm.trn (names only; not opened)

briefs.label: Ruined chapel dungeon
briefs.why: A single large chapel room gives a strong focal point for a dungeon floor.
briefs.keep: One dominant room with a clear plan; a tile-index map file.
briefs.change: Our own architecture (no church motifs); a different lighting mood; our own room count.

briefs.label: Creature sheet by table
briefs.why: Animation timing set in a table can be tuned fast and copied between creatures.
briefs.keep: Per-creature frame counts and frame rates for each animation state; a row per creature.
briefs.change: Our own state names and frame counts; a different number of states.

briefs.label: Storyboard still strip
briefs.why: A few wide stills plus cropped portrait frames can carry a short cutscene cheaply.
briefs.keep: Wide still for the scene; cropped portrait frames for the speaker; a fixed frame size.
briefs.change: Our own composition and aspect ratio; our own portrait framing.
briefs.ref: assets/gendata/cutportrw.clx and cutstartw.clx (names only; not opened)
